source.title: Alain Delon Style Breakdown | Why Everything Worked

tips.text: Know your measurements and what fits your body; a lean frame of average height looks best between tailored and relaxed, not skin tight.
tips.why: Clothes with shape and some ease look natural rather than tense.

tips.text: Looking sharp does not mean everything slim: let clothes have shape but also ease, with nothing too long, short, tight or heavy.
tips.why: Balanced proportions stay timeless.

tips.text: Wear clothes with ease: an open collar and pushed-up sleeves look relaxed; an outfit that looks too perfectly arranged reads as trying too hard.
tips.why: Comfort in your clothes is what makes style convincing.

tips.text: Keep accessories few and give each a purpose; don't bury simple clothes under extra details.
tips.why: Restraint makes an outfit look powerful.

tips.text: Ignore loud trends; wearing the same well-fitting basics properly beats chasing novelty.
tips.why: Simple clothes worn well never date.

tips.text: A plain light-coloured button-up shirt is the most versatile base layer; pick shades like light blue that flatter your eyes and skin.
tips.why: It goes with everything and frames the face.

tips.text: Smooth cotton shirts look sharper and keep the collar in shape; linen shirts look relaxed and sunny.
tips.why: The fabric sets the mood of the outfit.

tips.text: When dressing formally, do it properly: a well-tailored oxford, quiet colours and everything buttoned as it should be.
tips.why: There is a time and place for relaxed details.

tips.text: Match the looseness of top and bottom: don't pair loose trousers with a tight shirt or the other way round.
tips.why: Consistent volume keeps the silhouette coherent.

tips.text: Higher-waisted trousers with a slight taper and the hem just reaching the shoe keep the leg line long and clean.
tips.why: Well-falling trousers make the whole outfit look more expensive.

tips.text: Own trousers in several fabrics, such as cotton twill, linen, chinos and denim, mostly in neutral colours; the same few shapes look different each time.
tips.why: Material variety multiplies outfits.

tips.text: Use contrast between shirt and trousers: a dark shirt with light trousers or a white shirt with dark trousers.
tips.why: Contrast gives an outfit definition.

tips.text: Jackets should be structured but not stiff, with clean shoulders and a length that frames the body; not so long it swallows you, not cropped for fashion's sake.
tips.why: A balanced jacket supports the outfit instead of dominating it.

tips.text: Fine-gauge knits that follow the body without clinging dress an outfit down while keeping it classy; avoid very chunky, oversized or clingy knits for this look.
tips.why: A clean knit keeps the standard high.

tips.text: Pick knitwear colours that contrast with the shirts you own: dark charcoal, black or grey knits over white and light blue shirts.
tips.why: Without contrast the outfit looks dull.

tips.text: Choose suit cloth with enough weight to drape; in summer, wear lighter linen and cotton suits in pale colours.
tips.why: The right fabric keeps a suit from looking flat or cheap.

tips.text: Wear a suit like ordinary clothes and stay relaxed in it; don't let it make you stiff.
tips.why: You should wear the suit, not the other way round.

tips.text: A patterned tie can bring life to a plain suit; plain ties look more precise.
tips.why: The tie sets the suit's mood.

tips.text: Find one pair of sunglasses that suits your face shape and style and wear it often.
tips.why: The right frame becomes a signature.

tips.text: Keep belts simple: plain black or brown leather with an understated buckle.
tips.why: A belt should hold the outfit together, not distract.

tips.text: Keep jewellery subtle and in one metal, and wear one simple watch on a leather strap.
tips.why: Understated details look classier.

tips.text: Loafers suit a relaxed Riviera style; espadrilles or moccasins can be worn without socks in summer.
tips.why: Soft slip-ons fit warm-weather tailoring.

tips.text: Swim shorts look classiest fitted and fairly short, around a 15 cm inseam, plain or simply striped; throw an open linen shirt over them.
tips.why: Plain, well-fitting swimwear keeps style at the beach.

tips.text: A hairstyle should match the mood of your clothes; work with your natural hair rather than against it.
tips.why: Hair is part of the overall look.

outfits.why: A tailored dark suit with a patterned tie and a trench coat of the right length.
